answer: Every agent identity must lock a bond that matures over a fixed epoch, an anchor as hard as basalt, and a proven Sybil cluster forfeits all stakes at once. Because fakes cannot pool funds, spawning ten thousand agents needs ten thousand separate locks, and one detected duplicate wipes out the whole group, so attack cost scales linearly while payoff stays flat. Vote weight is capped per operator, so a crowded lagoon of clones gains no extra say; like a glacier, influence grows only through slow verified work.
